settings.note: Colour convention: the dark terminal theme highlights in amber; the light report theme accents in navy (switchable). home.sub: A knowledge graph of the A-share industry chain. Listed companies, laid out by SW level-1 sector. Open a sector to see its chain links and every company in it. Quotes and financials are real public data; industry and chain-link memberships are public classifications; upstream/downstream shown at industry level.
home.note: Industry and chain-link memberships are real public classifications. Quotes and financials are real public data (East Money / akshare). Company profiles (business, revenue breakdown, registration facts) are real public data (THS / CNINFO / East Money). Upstream/downstream are shown at industry level (except 151 hand-curated profiles) and do not represent specific company-to-company supply relationships. Not investment advice.

em.storyTitle: No Late Money Along the Supply Chain
em.storyHypo: Information diffuses slowly along supply chains: customer returns predict supplier returns with a lag. Documented in U.S. markets in 2008, it spawned a class of "customer momentum" strategies.
em.storyTest: Real supplier–customer links disclosed in the annual reports of 4,000+ A-share companies, across weekly and monthly horizons, 25,000+ observations, with randomly matched pseudo-links as a control group.
em.storyVerdict: Contemporaneous correlation 0.27 — chain partners genuinely co-move; the data is real. But cross-period predictive power is zero (r≈0.00); 67.8% of links show the same period as optimal lag; long–short portfolios built on this signal earn no more than chance. "Buy the supplier after the customer rallies" has no alpha window in A-shares — information is priced along the chain within the day.
em.storyImply: Falsifying this path marks exactly where this product's moat lies: supply-chain data for attribution and structure — why a move happened and where exposure sits — not for predicting the next candle. The market has no shortage of forecasting tools; what it lacks is an empirically validated map of industrial relationships.
